newsitem.title: USA: Rock Hall of Fame ceremony moved to Cleveland hotel.
newsitem.headline: Rock Hall of Fame ceremony moved to Cleveland hotel.

text.p: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Foundation said Thursday it will hold its 12th annual induction ceremony May 6 at a downtown hotel.

The event had been planned for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, but the 150,000-sq.-ft. museum has no space large enough to accommodate 1,500 for dinner and the cost of setting up a tent would be prohibitive, the foundation said. The ceremony will instead be held at the Renaissance Hotel.
"It's unfortunate that we can't hold the ceremonies at the museum," Suzan Evans, executive director of the New York-based foundation, said in a news release.

Inductees will include the Bee Gees, Buffalo Springfield, Crosby Stills and Nash, the Jackson 5, Joni Mitchell, Parliament-Funkadelic and the (Young) Rascals, as well as bluegrass legend Bill Monroe, gospel singer Mahalia Jackson and record pioneer Syd Nathan.

Cleveland, where disc jockey Alan Freed first popularised the term "rock 'n' roll," was selected over several other cities as the site of the museum after the city proposed a public-private financing plan.

The $92 million museum opened in 1995, but this will be the first year the induction is actually held in Cleveland. Previous ceremonies have been in New York and Los Angeles, and Evans has said London is among other possible future locations.
